div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Protein sequence
One amino-acid string per target. Median 454 residues, longest 34,350.

div.style: color: rgb(16, 42, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
ESM-C 600M · 573,632,640 weights, all frozen
572 effective target units cannot fine-tune a model this size without fitting the targets rather than the binding.

div.style: color: rgb(16, 42, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Residue cache · 14.0 GiB
All 10,820 targets encoded once, offline. Re-encoding reproduces it bit-for-bit, which is what makes reuse safe.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Ligand SMILES
One string per molecule, standardised so the same compound always spells the same.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Line graph + knowledge
Each bond becomes a node. Two extra nodes carry whole-molecule facts: a 512-bit fingerprint and 200 computed properties such as size and greasiness.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
LiGhT · 8 layers, 8 heads, width 96
Each bond repeatedly looks at bonds up to five atoms away and updates itself. Its bond-to-bond attention is kept for iBAM.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Molecule summary → 288
Fingerprint node, property node, mean over bonds — three parts, never blended into one.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Pre-training — done, before any affinity run
Hide one knowledge node, rebuild it from the molecule plus the other.
540,166 molecules: training-only, so anything in a held-out set — sealed panels included — is excluded.
Held-out loss 0.2002, 48.8% under a molecule-blind guess.

div.style: color: rgb(6, 64, 43) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
The seam: what the ligand hands over
One vector per bond, plus two masks. The first says which entries are real rather than padding; the second says which may be drawn on a molecule. The two knowledge nodes are real — the protein attends to them — but not drawable. Conflating those two questions is what forced them to be discarded before.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Protein → 96
1152 numbers per residue, narrowed.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Bonds → 96
96 numbers per bond, normalised.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Summary → 3 × 96
Each part projected on its own, so the fingerprint is never averaged in with the computed properties.

div.style: color: rgb(90, 58, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Knowledge conditioning · FiLM · 74,496 weights
The molecule's global properties rescale every residue and every bond, rather than merely being appended at the end. A quantity that is only appended can be ignored; one that multiplies cannot. Starts as an exact no-op, so switching it off compares the same model rather than a different random draw.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Protein looks at ligand
Each residue spreads its attention over the molecule's bonds. Then 96 → 192 → 96, re-masked.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p: Two separate sets of weights, run side by side. Neither sees the other's output, and one is not the transpose of the other.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Ligand looks at protein
Each bond spreads its attention over the residues. Then 96 → 192 → 96, re-masked.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
One vector for the pair — 576 numbers in six blocks
Fused residues · fused bonds · the protein before fusion · fingerprint · properties · bond average. That pre-fusion block is a route to an answer which does not depend on attention having found anything useful.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Score only the endpoint that was measured
Kd, Ki and IC50 are different experiments and are never mixed. A measurement that does not exist cannot be given a stand-in value, because no such value is representable.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Exact measurements
Error below the laboratory's own repeat scatter is free: 0.945 Kd, 0.641 Ki, 0.671 IC50.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Censored measurements · 16.6%
Records saying only 'weaker than 10 µM'. Penalised for crossing the bound, never for landing anywhere inside it.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Lower-confidence records
Down-weighted to 0.25 and kept structurally apart, so they cannot influence the main term.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Which of two is better — built, off by default
Compares only inside one assay, and only when the gap beats that endpoint's repeat scatter. The spec's 0.5 margin is under every floor.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
iBAM — what the model looked at
Every attention map kept per layer and per head, unaveraged: 32 protein-ligand from fusion, 64 bond-bond from LiGhT.
Residue × bond is native, because a token is a bond; residue × atom is derived and labelled as such.
Rows always sum to one, so rows rank nothing — column totals are the orderable direction. The bond map is gated by a control asking whether it says more than 'things near each other are related'.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Ensemble
Three separately trained models; their disagreement is a rough confidence signal. Three passes over one model is refused in code.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Calibrated intervals
Split conformal on a slice held apart from training. Too few points to support the quantile returns a status, never an invented interval.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Is this input familiar?
Similarity to training molecules only, computed without looking at the ensemble — models can agree confidently about the unseen.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Benchmark lock
Refuses to score a model on the sealed panels when its training set overlaps them. Measured from the split's own records, not guessed from its name: random 60–100%, cold-target 66–69%, time-based 0% — the only one that qualifies. Opening is logged and cannot be undone.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Drug fishing — an evaluation, not a component
3,721 targets · 81,971 actives · 37,187 measured inactives · 1,926,939 property-matched decoys. Ranking actives against decoys is a question asked of a finished model, so it needs no tower of its own.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
What it would be told
Target, endpoint, the seed molecule, what the model attended to, and which part of the scaffold to preserve.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Discrete graph diffusion
Atoms and bonds corrupted to noise by category and denoised back, with the protected scaffold held fixed throughout.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Back to a real molecule
Decoded with RDKit, sanitised, scaffold re-checked by atom mapping. Validity reported before and after any repair.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p: Never shown the answer it predicts — unavailable at inference, and it would learn to copy. Sampling is not differentiable, so gradients stop here.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 312px; text-align: center; width: 312px;

span.p:
Planned: the full objective
Affinity + ranking + generation + measured-change terms. Only affinity and ranking exist today.

svg.text: BINDRA-v1 · 2,070,043 trainable parameters · solid = built and tested, dashed = planned
